title: Atlassian's AI surprise: More software developers, not fewer
excerpt: AI was supposed to kill developer jobs. Atlassian's latest results suggest it's creating more software builders, not fewer.
content_html:
One of the biggest fears about AI was that it would kill tech jobs and shrink the software industry.

The logic seemed straightforward. If AI made developers much more productive, tech companies would need fewer of them. That would mean fewer software subscriptions, known as "seats," because each worker typically has their own account.

Investors also worried that AI coding tools would enable companies to build more of their own software rather than buy it from established vendors.

The software giant Atlassian sat right in the way of these buzzsaws because it sells tools that help teams organize work, collaborate, and build software. That drove the stock down more than 50% in the first few months of 2026.

Now, the picture looks very different.

Atlassian shares jumped 35% on Friday after the company reported surging revenue, helped by growth in seats for its main Jira and Confluence products.

That suggests that AI is creating more roles for software developers, rather than killing tech jobs.

"There's going to be more developers in the world in five years' time than there are today," Atlassian CEO and cofounder Mike Cannon-Brookes said after the results. "Developer hiring will continue to grow."

"The cost of building technology is going down. The amount of technology we're going to build is going to go up," he added. "Those are the signals we see in our customers. The ability to grow that is huge."

This reminds me of something Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said a few years ago. He predicted AI would make writing software much easier, opening this skill to many more people.

"The programming language is human; everybody in the world is now a programmer," he said.

Atlassian is seeing this happen across its corporate customers. The company said seat growth wasn't just coming from software developers. Roughly two-thirds of Jira and Confluence users are now in roles such as human resources, finance, and legal.

"The number of people building technology that we don't necessarily call developers is also growing," Cannon-Brookes said.

In other words, AI may not be replacing developers. Instead, it appears to be expanding who gets to build software.

If that's right, the long-feared collapse in software jobs and subscriptions may never arrive. Instead, AI could create a much larger pool of people building technology, and an even bigger market for companies like Atlassian.

content_html_zh:
人们对人工智能最大的担忧之一是它会杀死科技岗位并缩小软件行业的规模。

逻辑似乎很简单。 如果人工智能使开发人员的工作效率大大提高，那么科技公司将需要更少的开发人员。 这将意味着更少的软件订阅（称为“席位”），因为每个员工通常都有自己的帐户。

投资者还担心人工智能编码工具将使公司能够构建更多自己的软件，而不是从成熟的供应商那里购买软件。

软件巨头 Atlassian 正好挡住了这些趋势，因为它销售的工具可以帮助团队组织工作、协作和构建软件。 这导致该股在 2026 年前几个月下跌了 50% 以上。

现在，情况看起来非常不同了。

周五，Atlassian 股价上涨 35%，此前该公司报告称，得益于其主要 Jira 和 Confluence 产品席位的增长，收入大幅增长。

这表明人工智能正在为软件开发人员创造更多的角色，而不是扼杀技术岗位。

Atlassian 首席执行官兼联合创始人迈克·坎农-布鲁克斯 (Mike Cannon-Brookes) 在公布结果后表示：“五年后，世界上的开发人员数量将比现在还要多。” “开发商招聘将继续增长。”

“建筑技术的成本正在下降。 我们要开发的技术数量将会增加，”他补充道。 “这些是我们在客户身上看到的信号。 成长的能力是巨大的。”

这让我想起了英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋几年前说过的话。 他预测人工智能将使编写软件变得更加容易，向更多的人开放这项技能。

“编程语言是人类的；现在世界上的每个人都是程序员，”他说。

Atlassian 看到这种情况在其企业客户中发生。 该公司表示，席位增长不仅仅来自软件开发商。 目前，大约三分之二的 Jira 和 Confluence 用户担任人力资源、财务和法律等职务。

“开发技术（我们不一定称之为开发人员）的人数也在增长，”坎农-布鲁克斯说。

换句话说，人工智能可能不会取代开发人员。 相反，它似乎正在扩大谁可以构建软件。

如果这是正确的，人们长期以来担心的软件工作和订阅量的崩溃可能永远不会到来。 相反，人工智能可以创造更多的技术人员，并为 Atlassian 等公司创造更大的市场。
